data.narrative:
Built Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing firm founded by Noah Ready-Campbell and Andrew Liang, has raised $112M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from two primary methods triangulated against a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company in the robotics sector, including firms at Series B and Series D stages such as Exotec ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), Dexterity ($1.6B), and Hadrian ($1.6B).

Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x multiplier to the $17M total-raised proxy, implying a $29M valuation. This method captures typical Series C-stage step-up dynamics but is mechanically conservative. Peer-median triangulation across seven same-sector comparables at adjacent stages yields a $1.6B implied value, with a $1.0B–$2.0B range. The peer set reflects heterogeneity in stage maturity: five peers operate at Series B, while two (Exotec and Hadrian) are Series D, creating some upward pressure on the median.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $25M to $1.9B, with a median of $839M. The wide spread reflects tension between stage-based fundamentals and sector-level peer pricing. Key uncertainties include revenue traction and customer concentration relative to peer benchmarks, plus the sustainability of recent robotics valuations given public-market headwinds. Specificity on Built Robotics' contract pipeline and gross margins would narrow this range materially.
